search_strategy: Chat-only task (no wiki/mail carriers in this arm). The agent dumped the whole #-channel export to /tmp/chat2.txt early and then relied almost exclusively on `grep -n -i -E '<keyword-list>' /tmp/chat2.txt | head -30` passes with progressively refined keyword lists (identity/run_hash/digest/stamp; prompt_func_hash/parse_func_hash/components/dataset_hash; response_format/system_prompt/generation_params; ALTER TABLE/migrat/schema), interleaved with `sed -n '<range>p'` reads of specific line windows once a grep hit looked promising. This found the large majority of remarks (35/44 clues+reversals, all 4 herrings and all 4 reversals) because most of them cluster tightly around a handful of keyword families (run_identity/component names/IDENTITY_BACKEND_PARAM_KEYS) that the agent's grep vocabulary converged on early (by transcript line ~3327 it already had the full component list, the backend_params allowlist, and the nocache hash shape). The misses cluster around two patterns: (1) remarks phrased without any of the technical keywords already in the agent's grep vocabulary (e.g. g4.r2.l1 'flake hunt', g4.r2.l2 'same label twice', g4.r1.l-retries-fork '40k rows' -- all natural-language incident narratives with no identifier to grep for), and (2) remarks that did land inside a `head -30`-truncated dump or a scrolled terminal-screen window but past the point the agent's Analysis actually processed (g4.r1.fix27, g4.r1.l-params-none, g4.r1.l-params-copy never surfaced at all) -- the agent moved on to the next keyword search rather than reading the full surrounding exchange for a grep hit that looked tangential. No BookStack/wiki search was needed since this task's remarks arm has none; the agent did check BookStack once (line 4036-4113) and correctly found nothing, then returned to chat.

notable: The single lost fact traces to exactly one implementation gap: `LLM.backend_params` returns `self._backend_params` directly instead of `dict(self._backend_params)`/a copy (transcript line 7079-7085), so mutating what a caller reads back also mutates the LLM's internal state. Everything else asserted in the same test function (resolved backend, backend_params=={} for None) passed.

The two remarks carrying this exact fact (g4.r1.l-params-copy, g4.r1.fix27) were the weakest-surfaced in the whole run: l-params-copy: 0 hits anywhere in the transcript; fix27: exactly 1 line, inside a `head -30`-truncated grep dump, immediately followed by an Analysis that does not mention it (line 5145 -> 5190).

A closely related remark (g4.r1.l-params-none, 'passed nothing and its None ... should be {}') was also only partially surfaced -- its opening line appeared twice (transcript 5144, 5530) but the punchline never did -- yet that particular sub-fact (None -> {}) was implemented correctly anyway, most likely from general defensive-coding convention rather than from having read the remark.

All 4 herrings and all 4 reversals were correctly surfaced and correctly resolved in favor of the reversal; the agent never followed a herring into shipped code (backend_params-whole-dict x2, uuid4-in-nocache-path, isoformat-segment-in-nocache-path all correctly reversed).
